enamel.note: Page ground. Re-declared per board colour: bottle #0c3b2a, sindoor #8a1d12, ink #16150f, peacock #0a5e66, aubergine #40194f.

enamel-deep.note: Recessed value: dark panels, input wells, scrollbar track.

enamel-lit.note: Light colour, not a surface colour. Feeds the sodium pool's lift tint.

board.note: The painted board, and all body copy on the dark ground at 70-90% alpha.

board-dim.note: The one disabled-state value: a board not yet painted.

gold.note: The single instruction colour. Also selection, caret, scrollbar thumb, focus ring.

signal.note: Cost and refusal, on the dark ground only. Never a large fill.

signal-deep.note: Darkened signal for signal-coloured text on the cream board, where bright vermilion fails 4.5:1. Declared only in the palette blocks, not in @theme, so no Tailwind utility exists for it in this build.

ink.note: Letterform shadow, text on cream, painted 2-3px borders, ink chips carrying gold type. Dividers at 15-30% alpha.

faded.note: Paint that lost its light: terminal colour of a cooling enquiry, and low-contrast dividers on the dark ground at 25-55% alpha.

display.purpose: Hero headline only. Always carries the painted ink-shadow and cream-highlight treatment.

headline.purpose: Section h2, capped at 20-26ch. Closing call runs larger at clamp(2.1rem, 6.4vw, 4.25rem).

devanagari.purpose: The Hindi line under a display or closing headline, in gold. One per section at most.

title.purpose: Panel and step headings on cream; definition terms in gold on the dark ground.

body.purpose: All prose. Lead copy steps to 1.125rem at sm. Measure capped 42-54ch.

label.purpose: Eyebrow lines on panels, table headers, status badges, chips, trade-strip items. Tracking widens as size drops: 0.06em to 0.18em.

arabic.purpose: Perso-Arabic script items in the language list. Layout must tolerate RTL.

numeric.purpose: Every price, clock time, phone number and benchmark figure, in both Anton and Mukta contexts.

shadows.name: panel-cream
shadows.purpose: The painted board laid on the ground. Paired with a 176deg white-to-transparent gloss gradient over the cream fill.

shadows.name: panel-dark
shadows.purpose: Recessed deep-enamel panel, same construction at lower gloss.

shadows.name: keyline
shadows.purpose: The inset ink-then-gold double border a real board carries. Only on surfaces that represent an actual painted board.

shadows.name: button-lift
shadows.purpose: Under the gold primary action only. Removed entirely when disabled.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Global focus-visible treatment, token-bound so it retints with the ground.

shadows.name: painted-letterform
shadows.purpose: Ink shadow down-right, cream highlight up-left. Type only, never blocks.

shadows.name: painted-letterform-gold
shadows.purpose: Gold variant of the painted treatment.

shadows.name: painted-letterform-signal
shadows.purpose: Signal variant: ink shadow only, no highlight.

motion.name: ease-state
motion.purpose: Button and swatch lift (2px translateY) and colour swaps. 150ms for swatches.

motion.name: cool
motion.purpose: The only looping animation: a timestamp going from gold with an 18px warm glow to faded blue. Staggered 0.5s per card. Removed under prefers-reduced-motion, with the faded colour applied statically.

motion.name: marquee
motion.purpose: The trade strip, zero gap, pauses on hover.

motion.name: hero-arrival
motion.purpose: Entrance animation, hero only. No section below the hero has an entrance.

narrative.overview:
Enamel on tin. The system is built from the hand-painted trade boards that hang above the businesses this product is sold to — banquet halls, studios, salons — and it behaves like paint rather than like glass. A dark enamel ground covers roughly 60% of any screen; a cream board panel carries the content that matters on roughly 30%; cadmium gold and vermilion are the signal, held to the remaining 10%. Light in this world is a single warm sodium-vapour pool from above, not a rim glow and not a gradient mesh. Depth comes from paint sitting proud of the ground: a gloss band across a panel's top edge, an offset cast shadow below it, and an inset ink-and-gold keyline where a real board carries its border.

Letterforms are the system's most load-bearing material. Display type is condensed caps with an ink shadow thrown down-right and a thin cream highlight up-left — the actual grammar a sign painter uses to make lettering stand off a wall. That treatment belongs to type and only to type; no block, panel, or button wears it. The page carries four scripts by design (Latin, Devanagari, Perso-Arabic, Malayalam) because the audience reads them, so type coverage is a structural requirement rather than a nicety.

The ground is user-selectable: six enamel grounds a real shop would stock, every one of them dark, because the cream lettering and the cream panels depend on a dark field to read. The palette switcher is part of the system, not a demo toy; every colour token including the signal-on-cream variant and the four ambient-light tints is redefined per ground. The build explicitly refuses the dark-SaaS treatment: no glass, no neon on charcoal, no violet gradient, no soft 12px radius everywhere.
keyCharacteristics: Dark enamel ground at ~60%, cream board at ~30%, gold and vermilion signal at ~10%
Zero corner radius on every surface; squared edges, painted borders
Painted letterform shadow and highlight on display type only
One fixed sodium-vapour light pool; no per-element glow
Six interchangeable dark grounds, each retinting the whole token set
Tabular figures wherever money or clock time appears
Motion is scarce: hero arrival, one cooling loop, one trade marquee

rules.name: The Dark Ground Rule
rules.body: Every ground in the system is dark. The cream board, the painted highlight, and the gold signal all depend on it; a light ground breaks all three at once. A new palette that is not dark is not a palette in this system.

rules.name: The One Instruction Rule
rules.body: Gold marks the single next action on a surface and the two places the brand speaks (the Devanagari line, the trade strip). If a screen has two gold calls to action, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Signal-On-Cream Rule
rules.body: Signal-coloured text on the cream board uses the brick variant, never the bright vermilion. Vermilion is for the dark ground only.

rules.name: The Light-Is-One-Lamp Rule
rules.body: Ambient light is one fixed sodium pool composed of three radial tints plus one foot-glow at the closing section. Individual elements do not glow, and no element gets its own halo.

rules.name: The Paint-Only-Letters Rule
rules.body: The painted ink shadow and cream highlight apply to type and nothing else. A panel, button, chip or image with a hard offset shadow is not this world — that is the costume version of it.

rules.name: The Script-Coverage Rule
rules.body: Latin and Devanagari run through Mukta; Devanagari display runs through Yatra One; Perso-Arabic runs through Cairo. A new surface adding a script must add the face, not let the browser substitute. Layout must tolerate RTL.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Prose carries an explicit max-width in ch. Nothing in this system runs full container width as a paragraph.

rules.name: The One Board Rule
rules.body: Related steps live on one panel divided by dashed ink keylines. Reach for a second panel only when the content is genuinely a different board.

rules.name: The Safe-Gutter Rule
rules.body: Horizontal padding and fixed-element insets are always max(<value>, env(safe-area-inset-*)). The audience is on a phone, one-handed.

rules.name: The No-Glass Rule
rules.body: No backdrop blur, no translucent frosted surfaces, no neon rim light. Depth is gloss, highlight and cast shadow — the properties of wet enamel.

rules.name: The Keyline-Means-Board Rule
rules.body: The inset ink-and-gold keyline marks a surface that represents an actual painted board. A generic content panel gets the gloss and the cast shadow without it.

rules.name: The Zero-Radius Rule
rules.body: Nothing in this system has rounded corners. A radius on a panel, button, chip or avatar reads as a web app and breaks the material.

rules.name: The Border-Does-The-Work Rule
rules.body: Separation comes from a painted rule — 2–3px solid for structure, dashed ink for internal division — not from radius, not from a drop shadow between siblings.

rules.name: The One-Arrival Rule
rules.body: Entrance animation happens once, on the hero. Sections below do not fade in as you scroll. A page where every section arrives is a page that never settles.

dos: Do keep the ground dark, the cream board at roughly 30% of the surface, and gold plus vermilion inside roughly 10%.
Do use the painted shadow-and-highlight treatment on display and headline type, and only there.
Do set every surface at zero radius and let 2–3px painted borders and dashed ink rules do the separating.
Do use the brick signal variant for signal-coloured text on the cream board, and bright vermilion only on the dark ground.
Do put the primary action on the bottom edge of the board that carries the number, above a solid 2px ink rule.
Do set every price, time, phone number and benchmark figure in tabular figures.
Do cap prose measure in ch and set each language's text in the font that covers its script.
Do read every colour, including browser-chrome colours, from the palette tokens so a new ground retints the whole surface.
Do give any new looping or revealing animation a prefers-reduced-motion branch that preserves the meaning statically.
Do draw new icons as authored SVG at 1.75–2.25px stroke with square caps.
donts: Don't introduce a light ground. The cream board, the painted highlight and the gold signal all fail on one.
Don't put a radius on anything. No panel, button, chip, input or avatar.
Don't give a panel, button or image a hard offset shadow — that treatment belongs to letterforms. Panels get gloss plus a soft cast shadow.
Don't add backdrop blur, frosted glass, neon rim light, or a violet gradient. The build exists to refuse the dark-SaaS page.
Don't put two gold calls to action on one surface.
Don't use bright vermilion as a large fill, or as text on cream.
Don't add a per-section entrance animation, a per-element glow, or a second ambient light source.
Don't ship an icon from a library or a Unicode glyph where an icon belongs; the icon set is authored SVG.
Don't route the @theme font families back through next/font's var(--font-*) variables — that indirection silently fell back to system faces.
Don't add a system display face or a generic sans as a display fallback beyond the chain already set.
Don't split a sequence of related steps into separate cards when one divided board will carry them.
knownInconsistencies: signal-deep has no utility: the token is declared only inside the :root[data-palette] blocks and never in @theme, so Tailwind generates no text-signal-deep or bg-signal-deep class. The pipeline's 'today' lines, the comparison's cross marks, and the status section's 'now' badge and 'nothing to log into' chip ship with no colour applied and inherit instead. The token's intent is correct and is recorded; the wiring is not. Fix by adding --color-signal-deep to @theme, not by changing the usages.
One hard-coded green: the comparison's affirmative tick uses a literal #1b6b3a, outside the palette, which does not retint with the ground. It is not a system token and should not be copied.

Vestigial shadcn token block: the default shadcn/Radix neutral scale (--background, --primary, --chart-*, --sidebar-*, light and .dark) is still declared in globals.css and referenced by @theme inline, but no shipped surface uses it. Dead weight, not a second system.

Duplicated colour declarations: the enamel tokens are declared twice, once in @theme and again in the default :root palette block. The palette block is the effective source of truth for Cobalt; the @theme copy exists so Tailwind generates the utilities.
